name: Pontius Pilate
charge: Condemning a man he had three times pronounced innocent
summary: Pilate found no fault in him, said so three times, was warned by his wife's dream, and offered the crowd Barabbas instead. When they threatened that he was not Caesar's friend, he washed his hands, said, I am innocent of the blood of this just person, and delivered Jesus to be crucified.
offense: The judge who justifies the wicked and condemns the just is an abomination; the judge who follows a multitude to do evil is forbidden by name. He knew, he said so, and he signed. Water does not answer for a sentence.
judgment: Scripture pronounces nothing on Pilate personally; Acts names him with Herod and the Gentiles and the people of Israel as gathered together against the Lord's holy child, to do whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel determined before to be done. Paul cites his court as the place where Christ witnessed a good confession.

entries.commentary: They accuse him of perverting the nation and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, and Pilate says, I find no fault in this man. Matthew's account gives the reason he could see it: he knew that for envy they had delivered him.

Herod was exceeding glad, hoping to have seen some miracle done by him, and questioned him in many words, but he answered him nothing. He had nothing to say to that house. Its head had sought his life as a child, and this one had beheaded John.

Pilate says a third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him. He knew the man was innocent and gave sentence anyway. Barabbas, cast into prison for sedition and murder, is released, and Jesus is delivered to their will.

Simon a Cyrenian is laid hold upon and made to bear the cross after him. Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children. If they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

Two malefactors, criminals, are led with him to be put to death, and they crucified him at the place called Calvary. Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. The superscription written over him in Greek, Latin and Hebrew reads, This is the King of the Jews.

One malefactor railed on him; the other rebuked him, took the blame of his own deeds, and said, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. That man repented at the last hour, and was answered, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

There was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour, and the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst. The rending of the veil is a sign. What stood between the holy place and the holiest was opened, and the sacrificial service under the first testament was coming to its end.
The centurion glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man, and all the people that came together to that sight smote their breasts and returned.

Joseph of Arimathaea, a good man and a just, had not consented to their counsel and deed, and begged the body and laid it in a sepulchre hewn in stone. He was buried the same day, which is the custom written in the law. There is no waiting days over a body. The women returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment. That is written after the death, in the new testament.

As they spake unto the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them, grieved that they taught the people and preached through Jesus the resurrection from the dead. The Sadducees, Pharisees, elders, and chief priests were the religious leaders of that day, and they are the same religious leaders today: your Creflo Dollars, your TD Jakes, your Joel Osteens, your Gino Jennings, speaking the same things they spoke back then. The Sadducees were the upper class, the wealthy priestly and merchant families, moved by political and economic position. They came under the influence of Hellenism the same way today's pastors come under the influence of Americanism, preaching a prosperity and a political gospel and adopting their own man-made traditions. They were grieved because the teaching pulled the people, the money, and the control away from them. It is jealousy, envy, and the inability to guide the people, the same reason these pastors avoid a real sit-down with someone who actually knows the scriptures. The Sadducees did not even believe in the resurrection, yet they used scriptures they did not believe to try to confound Christ, the same way Christians and five-percenters take our scriptures they reject and use them to try to confound us. -

They laid hands on them and put them in hold unto the next day. The spirit that was on the Pharisees is being activated again, and everyone plays their role again in this lifetime; just as the disciples are back in the truth, the chief priests, Sadducees, and Pharisees are back too, saying the same things they said before. They insist Christ broke the Sabbath even though Peter and Paul testified that Christ did no sin, which shows the same spirit that was on the Pharisees is on the Christian pastors. The work the Sabbath forbids is occupational labor, not healing or picking corn to eat, and their real motive was envy, because the disciples gathered and unified the people and their control and money were being touched. -

Howbeit many of them which heard the word believed, and the number of the men was about five thousand. Many still hear and believe today, and it is mainly black men leaving the dead churches, because the church gives them no purpose, no structure, no discipline, and no position to lead, teaching them to be docile and subservient. This five thousand disproves the Christian claim that the Jews all rejected Christ. He came unto his own, meaning the religious leaders, the builders, the chief priests and rulers whose job was to guide the nation, and only those upper echelons rejected him, while thousands of the people believed and were zealous of the law. -

On the morrow the rulers, elders, and scribes, with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, and Alexander, and the kindred of the high priest, gathered together at Jerusalem. Annas had been high priest around 6 to 15 AD and kept the title even after the Romans ejected him, while Caiaphas, his son-in-law, was the official high priest the year Christ was killed. These were the very persons who procured the death of Christ. Caiaphas prophesied that one man should die for the people, speaking not of himself but from the prophecies he knew in [Isaiah 53](/bible/isaiah/53) and the Psalms. That nation he must die for is Israel, and "not for that nation only" means Christ would also gather the children of God scattered abroad, the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles the Christians claim. -

When they had set them in the midst, they asked by what power or by what name have ye done this, and Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said unto them, ye rulers of the people and elders of Israel. The conversation is still to Israel, always the Israelites. Being filled with the Holy Ghost did not mean Peter was shaking, sweating, or speaking in tongues; it means he was filled with the wisdom to speak with poise before the rulers. When you are brought before the synagogues, magistrates, and powers, the Holy Ghost teaches you in that same hour what to say, the way brother Abiel spoke eloquently in court and was released. You must be wise as a serpent and harmless as a dove, and the wisdom of God will speak through you. Peter, Paul, John, and Christ all went to the rulers and builders of the people, not to the white church, the mosque, or the temple of Zeus. Our job is to go to the scribes, Sadducees, Pharisees, and religious leaders of our own captivity to reason and win some, not to the same people who raped, robbed, drugged, and miseducated us and would never give up their power. This is why bishop gave the order to go to these Christian pastors. -

If we this day be examined of the good deed done to the impotent man, by what means he is made whole; be it known that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom ye crucified, whom God raised from the dead, this man stands here before you whole. Examine our good deeds the same way: taking brothers off the streets from drug dealing, gang banging, killing, and stealing; taking sisters out of prostitution; putting black households back together; keeping children from being aborted; keeping men out of prison. What did the disciples do wrong but heal the impotent man? Any time there is a good deed the Pharisees still attack, which shows the hardness of our people's hearts. It was never about the nation or the people; it was about their own vainglory, position, power, and authority.

This is the stone which was set at naught of you builders, which is become the head of the corner. It was the builders' job to build and bind the nation, to raise up the tabernacle of David, to bind the brokenhearted, and to feed the flock, but when the stone, Christ, came, jealousy and vainglory arose and they rejected him. The kingdom is therefore taken from them and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits. Christ is a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, because men stumble at his location, his upbringing, his appearance, and his low social class. He came from the same hoods we came from, from your Philadelphias, your Detroits, the south side of Chicago, so the Most High confounds the wise by the foolish and chooses the base and the underdog, the way he chose David, not the Creflo Dollars, the TD Jakes, the Cornel Wests, or the Umar Johnsons who already have a following and would take the glory for themselves. This is how you know God is working with us, taking men called nobody and setting them before princes. Christ is also a sanctuary, a place of refuge and comfort from the world, from crime, hatred, and murder, and he gives our people a purpose, which is what everybody is looking for. Simeon said the child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and the "own" that received him not is the fall of the scribes, Sadducees, and chief priests. -

Neither is there salvation in any other, for there is none other name under heaven given among men whereby we must be saved. Christians reduce this to saying the words "in the name of Jesus," but "none other name" means no other power or authority was given to any man; that authority was given to Christ alone, so there is no salvation in Moses or Elias, only through Christ. You cannot sneak into the kingdom through Islam, the Nation of Islam, Jehovah's Witnesses, Mormonism, Pentecostalism, Seventh-day Adventism, the Baptists, or Buddhism. Whoever climbs up some other way is a thief and a robber trying to sneak in without laboring; you must enter by the door, which is Christ. -

When they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled and took knowledge of them that they had been with Jesus. The rulers saw these men were not slick, cunning, and crafty like themselves; they were bold, coming as if straight off a plantation and a field, not the regular church men. That boldness is the natural animation of the Holy Spirit, not something you force or make up. Brothers who teach weak, like the Christian pastors, with no power and no conviction, are lacking the Holy Spirit. You cannot push the spirit out; when you keep the Most High's laws and stay in the scriptures, the spirit animates your teaching with boldness, the way Christ taught with authority and not as the scribes. People who call us hostile have simply never seen a man of God speak with the Holy Spirit. Peter was fearless and intrepid, a man who drew a sword and cut off the man's ear, which was not the first time he used it; he came from the streets, and we have brothers with that same posture. They took knowledge the disciples had been with Christ because you take on the attributes and characteristics of whoever you surround yourself with, and the disciples all spoke the same thing as Christ. -
Beholding the man which was healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it. The living proof of the miracle was standing right there, and the rulers had no answer.

They commanded them to go aside out of the council and conferred, saying what shall we do to these men, for a notable miracle has been done by them and we cannot deny it; but that it spread no further among the people, let us straitly threaten them and command them not to speak in the name of Jesus. It was never about the miracle but about losing their power and their seat of authority, and you have to be that wicked to witness the great works and still plot against the men who did them. Satan cannot cast out Satan, so they knew the miracle was of the Most High; yet the same way they consulted to put Lazarus back to death after Christ raised him, they chose to threaten the disciples rather than glorify God. That level of hatred, envy, and emulation is what the religious leaders had for the people. The Pharisees were divided over Christ, some saying he is not of God because he healed on the Sabbath, others asking how a man that is a sinner could do such miracles. That same division will bring people out of the Christian church to examine the matter and repent based on our works. -

Peter and John answered, whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye, for we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard. Having further threatened them, the council let them go, finding nothing how they might punish them because of the people, for all men glorified God for the man who was healed, who was above forty years old.

Being let go, they went to their own company and reported all, and they lifted up their voice to God with one accord: Lord, thou art God who made heaven and earth; why did the heathen rage and the people imagine vain things; the kings of the earth stood up and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ. Against the holy child Jesus, Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles, and the people of Israel were gathered together, and this same thing is going to happen all over again. Their prayer was for boldness to speak the word and that signs and wonders be done, so if you lack the Holy Spirit, your prayer should be that the Most High put it in you, for he gives it freely. When they had prayed, the place was shaken, they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness. -

The multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul, and neither said any of them that ought he possessed was his own, but they had all things common. They did not cleave to materialistic things; when you come into the truth those things lose their importance and your objective becomes how you can support the truth. This is the establishment of a community, for community comes from common. With great power the apostles gave witness of the resurrection, and great grace was upon them all; neither was there any that lacked, for as many as owned lands or houses sold them and laid the money at the apostles' feet, and distribution was made to every man according as he had need. This was not a prosperity doctrine where you give to get rich; you give so that when one lacks, all supply his need, whether food, an eviction, or a proper burial. The church was the epicenter and hub of the community, and the arms, not tithes, circled through it and were distributed according to each man's need. Joseph, surnamed Barnabas, a Levite of Cyprus, sold his land and laid the money at the apostles' feet; this is the same Barnabas who later traveled with Paul, and even as an apostle he gave arms. Every ranked man should give arms as a testament of his faith and leadership, even while spending his own money to travel and teach. --- Topics: [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Thou shalt not raise a false report, nor put thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness: basically, thou shalt not lie. If you did not see it, do not make up a story like you were there; keep your mouth shut. Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause. This deals with judgment: do not be a respecter of persons because a man is poor, as if he is automatically wrong when he brings a matter against a rich man. The judges were charged to hear the small as well as the great. In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again; if thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt surely help with him. This enemy that hates you is your brother, your own nation, not the other nations as [Matthew 5:44](/bible/matthew/5#v44) is misconstrued to mean. [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) proves it, saying the same law with thy brother in the place of thine enemy: thou shalt not see thy brother's ox or sheep go astray; in any case, no matter how you feel, bring them again unto thy brother. And if thou know him not, keep it in thine own house until thy brother seek after it. He is still your brother even if you never grew up with him; that is real love for your own people. Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) and [Leviticus 19:17-18](/bible/leviticus/19#v17) in your hip pocket with this verse.

Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause: verse six explains verse three again in case you did not catch it, do not be partial in judgment. Keep thee far from a false matter; the innocent and righteous slay thou not, for the Most High will not justify the wicked. Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous: do not take a bribe when it comes to judgment; be upright and honest.

Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger, for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. This is speaking about us, as [Exodus 22:21](/bible/exodus/22#v21) already laid out with [Leviticus 25:35](/bible/leviticus/25#v35).

Six years thou shalt sow thy land, but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still, that the poor of thy people may eat, and the beasts of the field after them; likewise the vineyard and the oliveyard. That is mercy from the Lord: in the seventh year the land itself fed the poor. The seventh year ties into the count of the jubilee: seven sabbaths of years to the forty-ninth year, and in the fiftieth year no plowing of the land, which the law takes up later.

Six days do thy work, and on the seventh day rest, that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid and the stranger may be refreshed. The stranger here can be another nation working for you: they too get their due rest on the sabbath. When the Lord sets Israel back up to rule, the nations will kick and scream at first, but once these laws are applied there will be righteousness reigning over the earth like they have never seen, and all will be refreshed on the sabbath, spiritually and physically.

Make no mention of the name of other gods is not saying you cannot pronounce the names Buddha, Allah, Krishna, Ra. Christ himself named Beelzebub, the chief of the devils, a name derived from the Philistine god of Ekron, and Christ did no sin; so the verse cannot mean the bare saying of a name. The Lord says this same thing three ways in this one chapter, and the other two places show the meaning: verse 24, thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works; and verses 32 and 33, thou shalt make no covenant with them nor with their gods, for if thou serve their gods it will surely be a snare unto thee. Make no mention means do not learn how to serve and worship them. Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year: all the males appeared before the Lord God three times in the year. The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover, kept in the time appointed of the month Abib, the first month of the year, as it is written, the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover. None shall appear before me empty: you could not come empty-handed. You brought the tenth of your oil, your wine, whatever was required, for the priests to replenish the storehouses. The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths.

Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning. The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk: the Lord repeats what was read at [Exodus 22:30](/bible/exodus/22#v30), that the young one was not to be taken too young and too soon; it stayed its seven days with his dam before it was given.

Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, obey his voice, provoke him not, for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him. That Angel is speaking of Christ. If thou indeed obey his voice, I will be an enemy unto thine enemies and an adversary unto thine adversaries. These enemies are not the same enemy of verse four: the enemy of verse four is your brother whom you must help and shew mercy; these enemies in verse 22 the Lord himself deals with and destroys for you.

The Angel goes before Israel unto the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, to cut them off. Thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works, but utterly overthrow them and quite break down their images. Serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, take sickness away from the midst of thee, none casting their young nor barren in the land, and the number of thy days he will fulfil. He drives the nations out by little and little, lest the land become desolate and the beasts multiply, until Israel be increased and inherit the land. The bounds are set from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river, the river Euphrates. That little sliver on the map today is not how big Israel is supposed to be: the land was to encompass all the way out to the Euphrates by Babylon, taking in parts of what is Iraq and Iran, and it will be filled one day.

Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods. They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee. This is the third way the Lord states the command of verse 13 in this chapter: no learning their worship, no serving, no covenant.

The fining pot and furnace remove impurities from silver and gold; likewise the Most High tries our hearts through trials to rid us of our impurities. We must go through trials and tribulations to gain the kingdom. This is why Christianity is false when it teaches you only have to accept Jesus in your heart to be saved forever. That is not what the scriptures say. Whoso mocks the poor reproaches his Maker, and gladness at another man's calamity does not go unpunished. Children's children are the crown of old men, and the glory of children are their fathers. Many of us grew up in fatherless homes, but we must not glory in a father's dishonor. Sisters should not speak evil of the man they chose to lie down with and bring in seed by, no matter how bad he is; children raised to despise their fathers must repent of it in this truth. Just as grandchildren crown the old, we glorify our Father in heaven and our forefathers by our repentance and return to righteousness. -

A gift is as a precious stone to him that has it; a well-instructed wife is one of these gifts, silent and loving, priceless and far above rubies. A silent and loving woman does not mean one who never talks; it means a shamefaced sister who is not a chest bumper, whose continent mind cannot be valued. He that covers a transgression seeks love, but he that repeats a matter separates very friends. Covering sin like Ananias and Sapphira, who conspired to lie to the apostles, is condemned. -

A reproof enters more into a wise man than a hundred stripes into a fool; the wise receive correction while the fool must be beaten. Whoso rewards evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house. That is everything right there. The beginning of strife is like letting out water, so leave off contention before it is meddled with; where envying and strife are, there is confusion and every evil work. Evil begins in the thoughts of the mind, so the strife the fool starts flows from an evil heart. -

He that justifies the wicked and he that condemns the just are both an abomination to the Most High. To justify the wicked is to wrest judgment and take a bribe. A bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous, and this perverting of judgment is something we suffer with as a people. Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who justify the wicked for reward; the reward usually comes as a financial gift or a place of importance. There is no point in a fool holding a price to buy wisdom when he has no heart for it. -

A friend loves at all times and a brother is born for adversity; a man void of understanding strikes hands and becomes surety before his friend. He that loves transgression loves strife, and he that exalts his gate seeks destruction; a froward heart finds no good and a perverse tongue falls into mischief.

A foolish son is grief to his father; Solomon understood the reasonings of men, which is why a wicked man takes a gift from the bosom to pervert judgment appears again and again in this one chapter. A merry heart does good like a medicine, but a broken spirit dries the bones. Wisdom is before him that has understanding, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth. Understanding comes only through keeping the commandments. This is why in Ecclesiastes Solomon gives the conclusion of the whole matter: keep the commandments, for that is the whole duty of man. -

A foolish son is a grief to his father and bitterness to his mother; to punish the just and strike princes for equity is not good. He that has knowledge spares his words, and even a fool who holds his peace is counted wise. Talking too much, especially without the words of the Most High, marks a fool. Let thy speech be short, comprehending much in few words; speak only when there is need of thee and hold thy tongue among great men. -

verses.text: Then said Pilate to the chief priests and to the people, I find no fault in this man.
And Pilate, when he had called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,

Said unto them, Ye have brought this man unto me, as one that perverteth the people: and, behold, I, having examined him before you, have found no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him:
No, nor yet Herod: for I sent you to him; and, lo, nothing worthy of death is done unto him.
I will therefore chastise him, and release him.
Pilate therefore, willing to release Jesus, spake again to them.
But they cried, saying, Crucify him, crucify him.
And he said unto them the third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him: I will therefore chastise him, and let him go.
And they were instant with loud voices, requiring that he might be crucified. And the voices of them and of the chief priests prevailed.
And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required.
And he released unto them him that for sedition and murder was cast into prison, whom they had desired; but he delivered Jesus to their will.
When he was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.
Pilate saith unto them, What shall I do then with Jesus which is called Christ? They all say unto him, Let him be crucified.
And the governor said, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out the more, saying, Let him be crucified.

When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.
Then answered all the people, and said, His blood be on us, and on our children.
Then released he Barabbas unto them: and when he had scourged Jesus, he delivered him to be crucified.
Pilate saith unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Jews, and saith unto them, I find in him no fault at all.
Pilate therefore went forth again, and saith unto them, Behold, I bring him forth to you, that ye may know that I find no fault in him.
And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Cesar’s friend: whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Cesar.
When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.
And it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he saith unto the Jews, Behold your King!
But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar.
Then delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away.
For of a truth against thy holy child Jesus, whom thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, and the people of Israel, were gathered together,
For to do whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel determined before to be done.
I give thee charge in the sight of God, who quickeneth all things, and before Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate witnessed a good confession;
Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment:
Keep thee far from a false matter; and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I will not justify the wicked.
He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both are abomination to the Lord.

lawsResolved.text: Doing injustice by justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous is an abomination and condemned by God.
You are not to twist, distort or pervert justice.
You shall not testify in a dispute for the sake of following the majority and thus pervert justice.
The judge that justifies the wicked and condemns the just is an abomination to God.
Judges shall justify the righteous and condemn the wicked.
Rulers are not to be a terror to good behavior, but rather to the wicked and evil doers.
You are not to be partial towards anyone or a respecter of persons in exacting justice, whether they be poor or rich, small or great.

text.text: Then said Pilate to the chief priests and to the people, I find no fault in this man.
And Pilate, when he had called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,

Said unto them, Ye have brought this man unto me, as one that perverteth the people: and, behold, I, having examined him before you, have found no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him:
No, nor yet Herod: for I sent you to him; and, lo, nothing worthy of death is done unto him.
I will therefore chastise him, and release him.
Pilate therefore, willing to release Jesus, spake again to them.
But they cried, saying, Crucify him, crucify him.
And he said unto them the third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him: I will therefore chastise him, and let him go.
And they were instant with loud voices, requiring that he might be crucified. And the voices of them and of the chief priests prevailed.
And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required.
And he released unto them him that for sedition and murder was cast into prison, whom they had desired; but he delivered Jesus to their will.
When he was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying, Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him.
Pilate saith unto them, What shall I do then with Jesus which is called Christ? They all say unto him, Let him be crucified.
And the governor said, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out the more, saying, Let him be crucified.

When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.
Then answered all the people, and said, His blood be on us, and on our children.
Then released he Barabbas unto them: and when he had scourged Jesus, he delivered him to be crucified.
Pilate saith unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Jews, and saith unto them, I find in him no fault at all.
Pilate therefore went forth again, and saith unto them, Behold, I bring him forth to you, that ye may know that I find no fault in him.
And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Cesar’s friend: whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Cesar.
When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.
And it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he saith unto the Jews, Behold your King!
But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar.
